name: Atrioventricular Septal Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Atrioventricular Septal Defect

criteria.description: Presence of a common atrioventricular valve instead of separate mitral and tricuspid valves
Defect involving the atrial septum and ventricular septum at the atrioventricular junction
Visualization of the atrioventricular septal defect on echocardiography
Clinical signs of congestive heart failure in infancy such as tachypnea and failure to thrive

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic evidence of a common atrioventricular valve and septal defects involving both atrial and ventricular septa
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings; genetic testing may support diagnosis in syndromic cases.

pathognomonic.notes: Leads to volume overload and heart failure

pathognomonic.symptomName: Combined atrial and ventricular septal defect
searchTerms: combined atrial and ventricular septal defects

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic systolic murmur at the lower left sternal border
searchTerms: heart murmur at lower left chest
characteristic murmur at left sternal border

common.symptomName: Congestive heart failure symptoms in infancy
common.notes: Includes tachypnea, diaphoresis, and poor feeding
Includes tachypnea and recurrent respiratory infections
searchTerms: too much blood flow to lungs

common.symptomName: Cyanosis on exertion or with crying
searchTerms: blue skin with activity or crying

common.symptomName: Hepatomegaly due to right heart failure
searchTerms: enlarged liver from right heart failure
irregular heart rhythms including AV block

occasional.symptomName: Edema due to congestive heart failure
searchTerms: edema due to congestive heart failure

rare.symptomName: Stroke or embolic events secondary to cardiac defects

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Polycythemia secondary to chronic hypoxia in cyanotic cases
imaging: Echocardiography showing common atrioventricular valve and septal defects
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical assessment
genetic: Mutations in genes related to endocardial cushion development (e.g., CRELD1)
other: Electrocardiogram showing left axis deviation and atrioventricular conduction abnormalities
Cardiac catheterization for hemodynamic assessment in select cases

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated ventricular septal defect without common AV valve
Absence of atrial septal defect component
No combined atrial and ventricular septal involvement
Overriding aorta and ventricular septal defect but no common AV valve

redFlags: Severe congestive heart failure in neonate
Development of pulmonary hypertension early in life
references: Maron BJ, et al. Atrioventricular septal defect. Circulation. 2020;141(15):e823-e839.
American Heart Association Guidelines for the Management of Congenital Heart Disease, 2022.
